installation:
## Installation

### Global (all projects)
```bash
bunx caspian-opencode-plugin setup
```

### Project-only
```bash
bunx caspian-opencode-plugin setup --project
```

Restart OpenCode. You should see toasts: **Caspian ready** → **Caspian inbox ready**.

## Configuration
Setup adds the plugin to `opencode.json` / `opencode.jsonc`:

```json
{
  "plugin": ["caspian-opencode-plugin"]
}
```

## Files Modified
- `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` or `opencode.jsonc` (plugin entry)
- `~/.config/opencode/commands/` (`/caspian:*` slash commands)
- `~/.config/opencode/skills/` (Caspian skills)

## Removal
Remove `"caspian-opencode-plugin"` from the `plugin` array and delete the copied `/caspian:*` commands and skills.

tagline: Recall what you already did in your other coding agents
description:
opencode remembers its own sessions. deja answers the other question: what you did in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Zed and fifteen more agents on this machine — including the months before you installed anything.

A local Go binary indexes the transcripts those agents already wrote to disk, and the plugin gives the model six tools over that index: recall past sessions by error or symbol, read the digest of one session, see which sessions discussed a file before you edit it, ask what this machine actually ran after a given error, and store a decision worth keeping. Recall also arrives unasked — once per session on the system prompt, and a relevance pass per prompt that stays silent when history has no answer.

BM25 over local files. No LLM, no embeddings, no network. Credentials are redacted at index time.
installation:
```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": ["opencode-deja"]
}
```

Then index once: `deja index`. The plugin ships the binary, but a deja you installed yourself (`brew install vshulcz/tap/deja-vu`, `go install`, or the install script) always wins.
